reason: The measurements are right and the remedy is wrong, and the remedy is what was submitted. Driven at 768x1024, 900x800 and 1023x900 with a moment open: the plate runs 12..756 / 12..888 / 12..1011, every grid child is exactly 480px wide at x=29, and 231 / 379 / 486px of plate sits empty. The page column (.b-two) runs 96..672 and 96..927 and the row titles start at 220. So far the finding is accurate. It then fails on its own premise. The fix says 'the stage is viewport-centred at these widths, so centring the plate lands it on the content column' - it does not. Applied verbatim (left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%); width:min(514px, 100vw-24px)), the plate lands at 255..769 at 1023 and 127..641 at 768, and the fields move from x=29 to x=272 / x=144. The grievance was that the fields sit 67px LEFT of the content column's edge; after the fix they sit 176px RIGHT of it and 52px right of the row titles they are editing. The stated defect is inverted and enlarged, not cured. Worse, the composition regresses. The sheet is deliberately docked, not modal - no scrim, the page scrolls under it. Screenshotted with the fix injected, the 514px plate stops reading as a bottom edge and becomes a card stranded mid-viewport with live plan showing on both sides and rows sliced mid-word by its edges ('Fina...', 'Cho...' at 1023; 'Final dress fitting' cut at 640 at 768), while --b-sheet keeps reserving a full-width band for an object that now covers half of it. That is the round-6 refutation about building a second modal editor arriving by a different door. On the reservation logic the finding is harmless but also uninformative: every consumer of the sheet's geometry is vertical only - --b-sheet is offsetHeight+24, keepInBand and the focusin escape read panel.getBoundingClientRect().top, scroll-padding-bottom and bottom:76px are vertical - and the plate's height is 559px capped or full-bleed, so nothing there breaks either way. Refuted on the fix, not on the arithmetic.
sharpenedFix: There is a salvage, and it is not this one. Keep the full-bleed docked edge (round 7's recorded call, and the screenshots say it was right) and move only the measure onto the page's own gutter: in the max-width:1023 branch add .b-edit { padding-left: 84px } and .b-edit .b-undo { left: 84px }. The page column's left edge is a constant 96px from the viewport across the whole 701-1023 band, so 84 + the 1px border + the existing 12px inset lands every label, field, stepper, segment, Done and Delete at x=97 - flush with the counts, the titles' column and the header above them - at 701, 768 and 1023 alike. Height stays 559px, so --b-sheet, the padding reserve and the 76px undo offset are untouched; 84+480+16 = 580 still fits inside the 677px plate at 701. That answers the one thing the finding actually measured (the fields sitting outside the page's left edge) without turning a docked sheet into a floating card.
